channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee rebounds as traders reassess hawkish Fed bets, oil prices drop
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) gains against the US Dollar (USD) after a flat opening on Wednesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Fragile strength hinges on Fed – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen notes EUR/USD has dropped to its lowest level since mid-2025 as Dollar strength is driven by rising US rate expectations and a higher probability of an October Fed hike than an ECB move.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Possibility of breakout above 101.80 hinges on US data
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) trades slightly lower against its key currency peers on Wednesday. At press time, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which gauges the Greenbacks value against six major currencies, is down 0.11% to near 101.28. Still, the asset is close to its two-month high of 101.64.

item.title: USD/JPY: Yen carry risks build into Q4 – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Daily notes that FX markets were surprised by Dollar strength in Q3, with EUR/USD and GBP/USD relatively subdued while USD/JPY saw “huge action” higher. The report warns this move may spill over into the Yen Carry Trade if it continues. Emerging Market FX is also slipping against the Dollar again, except for CNY, which is treated as a separate case.

item.title: ADP Employment Report expected to confirm a tight labour market in September
item.description: The Automatic Data Processing (ADP) Research Institute will release September’s monthly report on private-sector employment creation on Wednesday.

item.title: US core PCE inflation set to rise in August, pressuring the Federal Reserve
item.description: The United States (US) Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) will publish the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index data for August on Wednesday at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: TRY: Inflation and easing threaten Lira – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes USD/TRY has broken above 49.0, continuing a pattern of defended levels being breached in step-jumps. He downplays the broader systemic impact of a Turkish stock market scandal and instead highlights surging fuel-driven inflation and the prospect of CBT rate cuts. Ghose warns that an easing cycle in an inflation-vulnerable economy is the key risk for the Lira.

item.title: US Dollar: Strength persists on higher yields – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note the US Dollar remains strong despite softer US data, as rising long-dated US yields weigh on global risk sentiment and support the currency.

item.title: Euro remains depressed near yearly lows amid soft German data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) has trimmed some losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday but remains on the defensive, as data from the Eurozone fails to inspire, while France's ballooning debt starts to raise eyebrows.

item.title: Gold looks to build on gains above $4,200 on USD stays weak ahead of US PCE
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts some buyers for the second straight day on Wednesday, with bulls now awaiting sustained strength and acceptance above the $4,200 mark before positioning for an extension of the recovery from an eight-week low, touched earlier this week.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gains as US Dollar declines on easing Fed rate hike bets
item.description: NZD/USD gains ground after registering losses in the previous day, trading around 0.5650 during the European hours on Wednesday. The pair gains upward momentum as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following dovish remarks from Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams.

item.title: Japanese Yen trims part of intraday gains vs retreating USD as traders await US PCE data
item.description: The USD/JPY pair recovers a few pips from a one-and-a-half-week low, touched earlier this Wednesday, and trades just below the 157.00 mark during the first half of the European session, still down around 0.25% for the day.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitics and cracks drive Q3 surge – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank highlights a sharp Q3 rally in Brent Oil, rising from $73 to $104, with the 3-2-1 crack spread jumping from $17 to $62. The effective move from $90 to $166 underscores tightening energy markets.

item.title: Euro: EUR/USD risk reversal long setup – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities' Macro Research Insight recommends going long EUR/USD via a three-month zero-cost risk reversal, buying a 1.1610-strike call and selling a 1.11-strike put.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD trades flat around $61.50, US data awaited
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades in a tight range at around $61.45 during the European trading session on Wednesday. The white metal consolidates as investors await the United States (US) Personal Consumption Expenditure (PCE) Price Index data for August, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA tailwind seen fading – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur argues that market expectations for 1.5 further Reserve Bank of Australia hikes look excessive after softer August CPI data. While inflation remains above target, he highlights lagged effects of past tightening and weakness in the real estate sector. Baur concludes the RBA is likely to wait, leaving the Australian Dollar unlikely to gain additional support.

item.title: Euro holds gains against Canadian Dollar despite weak German Retail Sales data
item.description: EUR/CAD inches higher after posting modest losses in the previous day, trading around 1.6100 during the European hours on Wednesday. The currency cross gains support as the Euro (EUR) remains resilient following mixed German consumer spending data for August.

item.title: US Inflation: PCE revision seen as data clean-up – BNY
item.description: BNY Mellon’s Americas Macro Strategist John Velis argues that the upcoming PCE revision is a technical adjustment that will not alter the broader US inflation narrative. He highlights that portfolio management fees, which scaled with rising assets under management, distorted recent PCE readings versus CPI. The Bureau of Economic Analysis will shift to a labor-based methodology, improving the Fed’s preferred gauge without signaling real disinflation.

item.title: British Pound moves away from two-month low after UK Q2 GDP as USD retreats ahead of PCE
item.description: The GBP/USD pair attracts some buyers during the early European session on Wednesday and moves away from a two-month low, around the 1.3200 mark touched the previous day.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bright UK data helps the Pound to extend its recovery
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is bouncing strongly against the Japanese Yen (JPY) in Wednesday’s early London session, supported by the upward revision of the UK's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and a positive surprise in the Current Account.

item.title: Forex Today: Market focus shifts to critical US inflation and employment data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Wednesday, September 30:

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Declines below 1.4200, while staying technically bullish above 100-day SMA
item.description: The USD/CAD pair trades with mild losses near 1.4190 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. A rebound in crude oil prices provides some support to the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro recovers strongly against Japanese Yen, German HICP in focus
item.description: The Euro (EUR) has recovered a majority of its early losses against the Japanese Yen (JPY), but is still 0.14% down at around 178.13 during the European trading session on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro dips further against British Pound as German Retail Sales disappoint
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends losses for the fourth consecutive day against the British Pound (GBP) on Wednesday, as German retail consumption figures failed to cheer investors while the UK Q2 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was revised higher.

item.title: WTI drifts higher above $88.00 as Trump denies Iran sanctions relief
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the US crude oil benchmark, is trading around $88.30 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. WTI edges higher after US President Donald Trump denied he would be willing to ‌ease sanctions on Iran.

item.title: 1.3%: Germany’s Retail Sales rise by less than expected in August
item.description: German Retail Sales, a key measure of consumer spending, showed an upside in August. The consumer spending measure rose 1.3% month-on-month (MoM), according to official data released by Destatis, while it was expected to have increased 2.0%. In July, Retail Sales arrived at -3.4%.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Holds slight recovery from 0.6960
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) holds its recovery move to near 0.6972 from the day’s low of 0.6960 against the US Dollar (USD) during the early European trading session on Wednesday. However, the Aussie pair is still 0.18% down from its Tuesday’s closing price of 0.6985.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Tests 157.00 support after slipping below nine-day EMA
item.description: USD/JPY loses ground for the second successive day, trading around 157.10 during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Weakens below 1.3250, technical barriers sustain bearish bias
item.description: The GBP/USD pair loses momentum to near 1.3225 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. Surging US Treasury yields and the hawkish stance of the Federal Reserve (Fed) provide some support to the US Dollar (USD) against the British Pound (GBP).

item.title: Euro stays pressured below 1.1350, near YTD low vs bullish USD ahead of US PCE, Q2 GDP
item.description: The EUR/USD pair remains under some selling pressure for the third straight day and trades around the 1.1330 region during the Asian session on Wednesday, near its lowest level since May 2025, which it touched the previous day.
